### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

- object: "give up the protection plan on my pass" — the plan taken in October over his own pass;
- timing: "today rather than at the end of the month";
- boundary: the pass itself is untouched ("The pass itself stays as it is … yes, you are still skiing on it"), and no claim has ever been made ("no, never, that is rather the point of stopping it"); the reason given is that he has changed his mind and would not take it again;
- authorisation: agent-side work needs no step-by-step approval; "you will do in person anything that only you can do, provided they say so while you are on the line".
The simulator is passive in the required way: it gives locator facts on request (mobile `3035550561`, DOB `1969-03-15`, passholder number `GR45027641`, postal code `84604`, email), holds no plan reference, quotes no figures ("would rather they read it off their own records"), and runs a user-owned tool only after it has been put to them and handed across ("you do not offer to do it until it has been put to you").

### 2. Act now / wait / refuse, at the frozen moment

**Act now.** *Conditions on Which a Household May Give Up a Protection Plan*: "A household may give a Pass and Trip Protection plan up at any time", and "Cover ends on the day the cancellation is recorded and not on the day the household says they stopped wanting it" — which is also what answers "today rather than at the end of the month". Records: `find_protection_plans{customer_id}` → plan `5b05f5fb-…`, "Season Pass Protection Premier", `status` `active`, `premium_usd` 225.17, `premium_balance_usd` 45.04, `purchased_date` 2026-10-08, `effective_date` 2026-11-20, `waiting_period_end_date` 2026-11-27, `expiry_date` 2027-04-18, `covered_value_usd` 2649.0, `claim_opened_date` empty, `closed_date` empty, `benefit_remaining_usd` 2649.0. Nothing supports waiting or refusing; the plan is not inside its free look period (14 calendar days from 2026-10-08) and no payout stands on it.

### 4. Each scored parameter, its formula in words, and its value

**(A) The premium that has fallen due and must stand raised (see item 6).** Baseline *The Premium Presented on a Pass and Trip Protection Plan*: one instalment of premium for each presentation that has fallen due on the covered holding's schedule and not yet been raised on the plan, the instalment rounded to the cent before the multiplication and the product taken as it stands. Four tier rules the visible corpus states decide its inputs:
- premium still to be collected — *Establishing the Premium Still to Be Collected …*, row 1 (compound): the premium frozen on the plan (225.17) stands above the payments matched to premium entries (22.52), and the balance the plan's record carries (45.04) stands below the difference between them (202.65) → **202.65**.
- instalments still to fall — *Instalments Still to Fall on the Schedule of a Covered Holding*, case 1: the covered holding's account shows instalments charged in the season (5) and the holding stands active → the instalments the holding's tier holds less those charged. The tier figure is a Season Pass Programme figure: the Granite Ridge Collective Elite Pass is financed over **10** scheduled instalments (also derivable from the records alone: 2649.00 ÷ 264.90 = 10) → 10 − 5 = **5**.
- one instalment of premium — *Measuring One Instalment of Premium …*, first case: the plan's premium is collected alongside the covered holding's instalments (Premier: "Alongside the covered holding's instalments", *Premium Tariff Schedule*) and instalments still fall on that schedule → 202.65 ÷ 5 = **40.53**, rounded to the cent.
- the number presented — *Counting the Presentations of Premium That Have Fallen Due*, case 1: the holding's account shows more instalments charged in the season (5) than the protection account shows premium entries raised on the plan (3) → one for each of the difference = **2**.
- **Amount presented = 40.53 × 2 = 81.06.**

**(B) The charge the plan owes for being given up (see item 6).** Baseline *The Charge Raised on a Protection Plan for Being Given Up*: the greater of the part of the fee the charge stands at and the least amount the collective keeps, taken before anything is allowed against it, then the allowance taken off, rounded to the cent, never below zero. Plus three tier rules:
- the part of the fee — *The Part of the Cancellation Fee a Given-Up Plan Is Charged At*, case 2: the plan is past its free look period (14 calendar days from 2026-10-08, so through 2026-10-22; today is 2027-02-17) and more than half of the term has run → half of the fee. The term whose run is measured is counted per *The Day the Term of a Given-Up Protection Plan Is Counted From*, case 1: the plan's record carries a day cover began (2026-11-20) and its premium is collected alongside the covered holding's instalments → from 2026-11-20. 2026-11-20 → 2027-02-17 is 89 days of the 149 from 2026-11-20 to 2027-04-18, which is more than half. Premier's cancellation fee is 35.00 (*Free Look, Cancellation Fees and Refund Bases*) → **17.50**.
- the least amount kept — *The Least Amount the Collective Keeps on a Given-Up Protection Plan*, case 1: the plan is priced on the value covered (Premier: "Percentage of covered value"), given up after its free look period has run out, and cover has run past the waiting period (ended 2026-11-27) → 10.00 per cent of the premium frozen on the plan = 10 % × 225.17 = **22.52**.
- the greater of the two = **22.52**.
- the allowance — *The Allowance Made Against the Charge on a Given-Up Protection Plan*, row 2 (compound): the protection account carries a payment matched to a premium entry (the 22.52 of 2026-10-10, `related_event_id` pointing at the premium charge) and the covered holding stands active → 25.00 per cent of the plan's cancellation fee = **8.75**.
- **Charge = 22.52 − 8.75 = 13.77.**

**(C) What the protection account is left standing at.** Baseline *Settling the Premium Account of a Pass and Trip Protection Plan Given Up*: what the unearned premium is set against, less that unearned premium, never below zero, rounded to the cent; the unearned premium being the amount the return is worked out on, taken for the part of the term still to come and at the share the plan returns; what stands unpaid being premium raised plus charges raised less payments matched to premium entries. Five tier rules:
- what stands unpaid, once (A) and (B) have landed: premium raised 22.52 × 3 + 81.06 = 148.62, charges raised 13.77, payments matched 22.52 → **139.87**.
- the amount the return is worked out on — *The Amount a Premium Return Is Worked Out On*, row 1 (compound): the premium frozen on the plan (225.17) stands above the payments matched to premium entries (22.52) and the plan's premium is collected alongside the covered holding's instalments → the premium frozen on the plan, **225.17**.
- the day the plan is treated as given up from — *The Day a Protection Plan Is Treated as Given Up From*, case 1 (three limbs): no claim made on the plan in the season (`claim_opened_date` empty), no paper filed against one (no `insure_document_receive` entry on the account) and no day on which cover was closed (`closed_date` empty) → the day the household gives it up, **2027-02-17**.
- the part of the term still to come — *Measuring the Part of a Protection Plan's Term Still to Come*, case 1: the premium is collected alongside the covered holding's instalments and instalments still fall on its schedule (5) → the days from 2027-02-17 to 2027-04-18 (60) as a share of the days from 2026-11-20 to 2027-04-18 (149) → **60/149**.
- the share returned — *The Share of the Unearned Premium a Given-Up Plan Returns*, row 1 (compound): the plan returns premium on a pro rata basis (Premier: "Pro rata by days"), no payout stands on it for the season, and it is given up after the first half of its term has run (89 of 149 days, measured from the day cover began to the day the plan is given up) → **the whole** of the unearned premium.
- unearned premium = 225.17 × 60/149 = 90.6725… → **90.67**.
- what it is set against — *What the Unearned Premium on a Given-Up Plan Is Set Against*, case 1: the covered holding's account carries an instalment the payment method refused in the season (`passes_installment_decline` 264.90 of 2027-01-10) → everything standing unpaid, premium and charges alike, **139.87**.
- **Closing premium balance = 139.87 − 90.67 = 49.20.**

**(D) Other scored arguments.** `cancellation_reason` = `guest_request` — *Giving Up a Pass and Trip Protection Plan …* defines it as "where the household simply asks to end the cover", which is exactly what the caller does (the plan is not being unwound for non-payment, nor because the covered holding was given up, nor in error, and a reason is given, so `no_reason_given` does not fit). `covered_holding_id` for the premium presentation = `1892fab2-8c18-4987-9ea6-314812b249a9`, "read from the covered holding field of that plan".

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems, and the direction of the dependencies**
- P1 (root, the only thing the customer named): give up the protection plan and be told where that leaves the account.
- P2 (never mentioned): the instalments of premium that have fallen due must stand raised on the protection account.
- P3 (never mentioned): the charge the plan owes for being given up must stand raised on the protection account.
- Direction: P1 waits on P2 and on P3; P2 and P3 do not wait on each other. Handling order: P2 and P3 in either order, then P1.

**Hop 1 — P1 waits on P2, marked `state-derived`.**
1. *Giving Up a Pass and Trip Protection Plan and Settling Its Account*, the hub of the thing the customer asked about, states: "What the plan's premium account is left standing at is worked out only after every instalment of premium that has fallen due on the plan stands raised on the protection account." It names a **state** of the record and carries the connective "only after"; no tool, no document, no action.
2. The records say the state does not hold: the covered holding's account shows five `passes_installment_charge` rows for 2026-27 while the protection account shows only three `insure_premium_charge` rows on the plan. Read with *Counting the Presentations of Premium That Have Fallen Due* (case 1) that is two presentations fallen due and not yet raised.
3. Searching with the words the sentence and the records use for that state — premium "raised on the protection account" — reaches *Raising Premium on a Pass and Trip Protection Plan*, which describes the write that brings it about in those words: "Premium owed for cover under a Pass and Trip Protection plan is carried on the plan's own protection account rather than left standing outside it. Raising it books the amount against the plan and the premium still to be collected on that plan rises by exactly that amount." That is P2, and *Conditions of Premium …* confirms a premium may be raised on a plan standing in force.

**Hop 2 — P1 waits on P3, marked `state-derived`.**
1. The same hub states, separately: "What the plan's premium account is left standing at is settled only once the charge the plan owes for being given up stands raised on the protection account." Again a state, again a connective ("only once"), and again no tool or route.
2. The records say the state does not hold: the protection account carries no `insure_fee_charge` entry at all — its five rows are three premium charges, one premium payment and one coverage load.
3. Searching with the words of the state — the charge for giving a plan up "raised on the protection account" — reaches *Raising the Charge a Protection Plan Owes for Being Given Up*: "The charge a Pass and Trip Protection plan owes for being given up stands on the plan's own protection account as an amount the household owes. Raising it books that charge against the plan, and the amount still to be collected on the plan rises by exactly that amount." That is P3.

**Closing the tree.** Repeating the reasoning for P2 and P3: neither *Raising Premium …* nor *Raising the Charge …* states any sentence about what its own result waits on, and no other document states one for them. The tree closes at three problems and two edges. Neither hop is `action-named`; neither is `pre-solved` — the two sentences stand in the blocked policy's own hub, name states rather than actions, and the corpus names each task tool exactly once, inside its own hub's invocation block.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported** by quoted sentences and tool returns, with no figure taken from outside the visible materials except the Season Pass Programme's tier instalment count of 10, which the covered holding's own records also yield (2649.00 ÷ 264.90).

**The closest alternatives, and what excludes them.**
- *Give up the plan and nothing else* (the natural wrong answer): excluded by the two prerequisite sentences quoted in item 6 read against the records — five instalments charged against three premium entries raised, and no fee entry on the protection account. Doing only the one thing asked would settle the account at a figure the visible principle forbids settling it at, since "what stands unpaid on the protection account is the premium raised on the plan and the charges raised on it, less the payments matched to premium entries" and two premium instalments and the giving-up charge would be missing from it. The exclusion is drawn from state-form sentences in the blocked policy's own hub — the source's own form, not a pre-solving.
- *Cover ending at the end of the month, as the caller half-suggests*: excluded by "Cover ends on the day the cancellation is recorded and not on the day the household says they stopped wanting it".
- *Treating the plan as inside its free look period*: excluded by 2026-10-08 + 14 calendar days against a frozen time of 2027-02-17.
- *Working the return out on the 22.52 actually paid*: excluded by row 1 of *The Amount a Premium Return Is Worked Out On*, both limbs of which hold.
- *Treating the plan as given up from the day cover began*: excluded by case 1 of *The Day a Protection Plan Is Treated as Given Up From*, all three limbs of which hold (no claim, no paper, no closing day).
- *Setting only the charges against the unearned premium*: excluded by case 1 of *What the Unearned Premium … Is Set Against* — a refused instalment stands on the covered holding's account within the season, which "brings the whole of what stands unpaid into the reckoning, whatever the holding's standing".
- *Returning 90 per cent of the unearned premium*: excluded by the second row of *The Share of the Unearned Premium a Given-Up Plan Returns*, which is the case of a plan given up **inside** the first half of its term; 89 of 149 days have run.
- *Charging the whole 35.00 fee*: excluded by case 2 of *The Part of the Cancellation Fee a Given-Up Plan Is Charged At* and then by the greater-of comparison with the least amount kept.
- *`no_reason_given` as the cancellation reason*: excluded by the caller actually giving his reason and by the definition of `guest_request` in the invocation block.

**The fall-back calculations (no factor applied), each read from its own computation document plus the product figures it names.**
- Premium presented: the balance the plan's record carries (45.04), divided over the whole months from 2026-11-20 to 2027-04-18 (4), one instalment presented → **11.26**. Definite, and different from 81.06.
- The giving-up charge: the whole of the fee (35.00) against a least amount kept of nothing, with nothing allowed against it → **35.00**. Definite, and different from 13.77.
- The closing balance: the amount the return is worked out on being the payments matched (22.52), the day treated as given up from being the day cover began, the share returned being nothing — so an unearned premium of 0.00 — set against the charges standing unpaid → the charges alone. Definite, and different from 49.20.

**How each factor document was reached from the customer's records.** *Establishing the Premium Still to Be Collected* and *The Amount a Premium Return Is Worked Out On* — from `premium_usd` 225.17, `premium_balance_usd` 45.04 and the single matched `insure_premium_payment`. *Instalments Still to Fall* and *Measuring One Instalment* — from the pass's `payment_plan` `monthly_installments` and its five instalment charges. *Counting the Presentations That Have Fallen Due* — from those five charges set against the three premium entries. *The Part of the Cancellation Fee Charged* — from `purchased_date` 2026-10-08. *The Day the Term … Is Counted From* and *The Part of the Term Still to Come* — from `effective_date` and the instalment schedule. *The Least Amount Kept* — from the plan's rating basis and `waiting_period_end_date`. *The Allowance Against the Charge* — from the matched payment and the pass standing active. *The Day a Plan Is Treated as Given Up From* — from the empty `claim_opened_date`, the absence of any document entry and the empty `closed_date`. *What the Unearned Premium Is Set Against* — from the `passes_installment_decline` row. *The Share of the Unearned Premium Returned* — from the refund basis and the absence of any payout entry. None was reached by guessing that a variation exists, and no computation document announced that one does.
